invariant: Java preserves source identity for parallel same-endpoint transitions across both PlantUML and cgraph. CucaDiagramFileMakerSvek groups links with the same connections without changing their relative source order, GraphvizImageBuilder constructs SvekEdge values in that order, and Bibliotekon retains those values in insertion order. SvekEdge.appendLine emits each relationship as a separate DOT edge statement carrying a unique marker color. Before the cgraph DOT grammar creates an edge, endedge calls bindattrs for the statement, which binds its text and HTML attribute symbols into the edge schema; only then does newedge call agedge and apply the statement values. Graphviz may traverse or geometrically order the resulting lanes differently, but SvekEdge.solveLine recovers the spline belonging to each original link by its marker color. Rust must therefore reproduce the parser's bind-before-create lifecycle and retain the returned cgraph edge pointer as caller identity. Parallel route identity is neither endpoint-pair order nor left-to-right lane order; it is the source link attached to the schema-initialized edge instance that Graphviz routed.
causal_divergence: Rust currently creates each Agedge_t before agsafeset and agsafeset_html introduce that statement's edge attributes into cgraph's schema. Java's DOT path does the opposite: bindattrs registers arrowtail, arrowhead, minlen, color, and any HTML label before newedge allocates and initializes the edge. A direct probe against the vendored library reproduces Java's source-owned lanes when it parses Java's DOT, when node colors are removed, when nodes are renamed, when nodes are fixed-size, and when the parsed parallel edges are deleted and recreated after the attribute schema already exists. Changing only Rust's synthetic edge names to anonymous IDs leaves both heldouts failing, falsifying the initial name-based hypothesis recorded in the preceding account revision. The remaining causal difference is edge allocation before versus after schema binding. Sorting paths, reversing declaration order, or assigning by label width would discard Java's marker-based identity and overfit the observed two- and three-lane cases.
